title: Business sale or wind-down planning
summary: Unique to self-employed: your business may have transferable value, or it may not. Plan accordingly.
detailsHtml:
Does your business have sale value?

Service businesses built around a single owner's skill (consulting, freelancing, sole-practitioner law/accounting) typically have limited sale value — clients don't transfer reliably to a new owner. Businesses with systematized operations, employee teams, or recurring revenue (SaaS, productized services, subscription models) often sell for 2–8x SDE (seller's discretionary earnings).

If saleable: prepare 3–5 years in advance

Document systems and processes. Reduce owner-dependency. Build a leadership layer if practical. Clean up financials (separated personal/business, clear revenue tracking, audited or reviewed statements). Buyers pay materially more for businesses that "run without the owner."

If not saleable: plan a glide path

Phased reduction in client load, transition of remaining clients to peers, gradual wind-down. The retirement question becomes "when does my portfolio fully replace my income" rather than "when do I sell."
